newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end slightly off but uptrend remains.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end slightly off but uptrend remains.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended slightly lower on Thursday as the market lost strength late in the day, but analysts said the bolsa's uptrend remains.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares fell 0.15 percent to close at 76,558 points, after rising to 77,425 points earlier.

Market turnover surged to 755.6 million reais ($724.5 million) on increased foreign buy orders, which some traders say also reflect investors' move to avoid paying the CPMF tax which will take effect January 23.
Foreign investors under Annex Four rules will pay a 0.2 percent tax on starting and ending their stock investments.
Local analysts also attributed market weakness at the end of the session to a rise in U.S. 30-year long bond yields, which helped weaken U.S. stock prices.
Among top blue-chips, benchmark Telebras fell 0.57 percent to 87.40 reais. State oil company Petrobras ended off 0.8 percent to 186.50 reais.

State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce continued its uptrend, with traders still speculating on the stock despite confusion over reports of new copper and gold finds. The company's preferred stock closed up 2.13 percent at 24 reais.
The power sector index .IEE, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, rose 1.03 percent to end at 2,224 points.
